title_ar: الشيخ الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء يحاضر في الكويت عن دور المغترب في خدمة الأوطان
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew, President of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, Lectures in Kuwait on the Role of the Expatriate in Serving the Homeland
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة في الكويت بعنوان: " دور الجاليات المهاجرة في خدمة الأوطان" نظمتها رابطة الجالية الموريتانية بالكويت وذلك بفندق " كويت كونتينانتال"، بتاريخ: 18/05/2011.
تطرق الشيخ في حديثه إلى الفرص المتاحة للإنسان في هذه الدنيا، وضرورة استغلال هذا العمر القصير في العلوم النافعة والكسب الحلال.
وقال الشيخ إن الله تعالى قد كتب على بني البشر الهجرات في الأرض؛ ومن هذه الهجرات ما يكون طلبا للعلم والرزق، ومنها ما يكون هجرة هرب من الضيق والحرج وطلب للحرية.
وقد استطرد الشيخ في ذكر النماذج والأمثلة على هذه الهجرات، مسترشدا بهجرة الأنبياء عليهم السلام، ونماذج من المهاجرين الشناقطة.
وركز الشيخ في محاضرته على التوجيه للجالية لما ينبغي أن يتحلى به المهاجر من أخلاق حميدة، وما يضطلع به من دور فعال في خدمة وطنه ماديا ومعنويا، كما حث الجالية على أن تكون سفارة حسنة لوطنها في العلم والأخلاق.
وحذر الشيخ من السلبية والتكلس الذي يصيب بعض الجاليات بحيث تنفصل عن الوطن الأم ولا تندمج مع المجتمع الجديد وبذلك تصبح متذبذبة في انتمائها وتمثيلها.
ودعا الشيخ المغتربين والمهاجرين إلى الارتباط بالوطن وخدمته بكل السبل المتاحة كما دعاهم إلى تطوير أنفسهم واستغلال الخبرات والتجارب التي يتيحها التواصل مع الآخر من أجل الإسهام في إصلاح أوطانهم وتوعية مجتمعاتهم.
وقد كان للشعر والأدب حضوره رغم ضيق الوقت حيث لم يفوت الشعراء فرصة الترحيب بالشيخ والإشادة بمكانته وإسهاماته الدعوية والعلمية والإصلاحية.
وقد شهت المحاضرة حضورا بارزا من أفراد الجالية، كما حضرها بعض الضيوف من الأشقاء الكويتيين.
وفي نهاية المحاضرة تم إهداء درع تقديري للشيخ من طرف رابطة الجالية الموريتانية على الأدوار الكبيرة التي يضطلع بها فضيلته في التعريف بثقافة البلد وتمثيله في المحافل العلمية.
وقد نظمت المحاضرة من طرف رابطة الجالية الموريتانية في الكويت، ضمن أنشطة علمية وثقافية تقيمها الرابطة من أجل تفعيل جسر التواصل بين الجالية نفسها من جهة، وبينهم مع وطنهم من جهة أخرى.
لمتابعة المحاضرة اضغط هنا
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture in Kuwait entitled "The role of emigrant communities in serving their homelands", organised by the League of the Mauritanian Community in Kuwait at the Kuwait Continental Hotel, on 18/05/2011.

In his talk the Sheikh addressed the opportunities available to a person in this world, and the necessity of using this short lifespan in beneficial knowledge and in lawful earning.

The Sheikh said that God, exalted is He, has decreed migrations in the earth upon the children of man. Among these migrations are those undertaken in search of knowledge and of provision, and among them are migrations of flight from straitness and distress and in search of freedom.

The Sheikh went on at some length in mentioning patterns and examples of these migrations, taking guidance from the migrations of the prophets, peace be upon them, and from examples among the Shinqiti emigrants.

In his lecture the Sheikh concentrated on directing the community towards the praiseworthy character an emigrant ought to display, and the effective role he undertakes in serving his homeland materially and morally. He also urged the community to be a good embassy for its homeland in knowledge and in character.

The Sheikh warned against the passivity and ossification that afflicts some communities, such that they cut themselves off from the mother country and do not integrate into the new society, and so become unsteady in their belonging and in their representation.

The Sheikh called upon those living abroad and upon emigrants to keep their bond with the homeland and to serve it by every available means, and called upon them likewise to develop themselves and to make use of the expertise and the experience that contact with others affords, so as to contribute to reforming their homelands and to raising the awareness of their societies.

Poetry and letters had their presence, despite the shortness of the time, as the poets did not let slip the opportunity to welcome the Sheikh and to acclaim his standing and his contributions in calling people to Islam, in scholarship and in reform.

The lecture [drew] a notable attendance from members of the community, and some guests from among the Kuwaiti brethren also attended.

At the end of the lecture a shield of appreciation was presented to the Sheikh by the League of the Mauritanian Community, for the great roles his eminence undertakes in making the country's culture known and in representing it in scholarly gatherings.

The lecture was organised by the League of the Mauritanian Community in Kuwait, as part of scholarly and cultural activities the League holds in order to activate the bridge of communication among the community itself on the one hand, and between them and their homeland on the other.

Recorded in source_download_link and omitted from body_en. The substance of what the Sheikh actually said is in that recording; this record is only a news desk's paraphrase of it.

flags.context: مسترشدا بهجرة الأنبياء عليهم السلام، ونماذج من المهاجرين الشناقطة
flags.note: 'الشناقطة' denotes the scholarly tradition and people of Shinqit and is not simply a synonym for the modern nationality, which the same paragraph distinguishes from it. The transliterated form is kept, matching its use in the style guide's own description of the Sheikh.

translator_notes: This is a news report written by the site's news desk, not a text by the Sheikh. Everything attributed to him arrives at second hand and in summary, even where the report uses quotation marks. The site must render it as reportage.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the event took place or when the report was written.
The report does date the lecture itself, to 18 May 2011, four days before the CMS timestamp. That in-body date is evidence; the timestamp is not.

No word of the Sheikh's is quoted directly anywhere in this record — every sentence attributed to him is the news desk's summary in reported speech. The English keeps the reporting verbs visible ('the Sheikh said that…') rather than smoothing them into direct assertion.
'الوطن' and 'الأوطان' are rendered 'homeland' throughout rather than 'nation' or 'country', which would import a political register the Arabic does not carry here.
